newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan coastguard believes tanker leaks stopped.
newsitem.headline: Japan coastguard believes tanker leaks stopped.

text.p: Japan's coastguard said on Wednesday it believed leaks from two ruptured oil storage tanks in a supertanker that struck a reef in Tokyo Bay had stopped.

"We believe the oil has stopped leaking from the ship but we have not been able to confirm that," said Kenji Koyanagi, spokesman for the coastguard's regional headquarters in Yokohama, south of Tokyo.
"But the ship would not have been able to move if it were still leaking," Koyanagi said.
The tanker, the Panamanian-registered Diamond Grace, was moving under its own power and was expected to take about an hour to reach Kawasaki Sea Berth in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo.

The 259,999-deadweight tonne tanker struck the undersea Nakanose reef off Yokohama, one of the most well-known undersea hazards in Tokyo Bay, on Wednesday morning. At its shallowest point, the reef is only 12 metres (37 feet) below the surface.
The ship leaked an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil, making it the worst ever oil spill accident in Japan.
